stem.text: Oil is pumped into a storage drum at a rate of R(t) gallons per hour, where R is a positive function and t is measured in hours. Using correct units, interpret the meaning of \( \int_{1}^{10} R(t)\,dt \) in the context of the problem.

answer_key.label: It is the total amount of oil pumped into the drum from \( t = 1 \) to \( t = 10 \) hours, measured in gallons.

worked_solution.text: R(t) is a rate measured in gallons per hour, so integrating it over time multiplies by hours and gives an amount in gallons.
worked_solution.rule_named: units of a definite integral of a rate

worked_solution.text: The limits run from \( t = 1 \) to \( t = 10 \) hours, so \( \int_{1}^{10} R(t)\,dt \) is the total amount of oil pumped into the drum from \( t = 1 \) to \( t = 10 \) hours.
worked_solution.rule_named: integral of a rate is the accumulated change

worked_solution.text: The units are gallons per hour times hours, which is gallons.
